Author Names: Y. Wei, J. Jang-Jaccard, F. Sabrina, A. Singh, W. Xu, S. Camtepe
Title of the Paper: Reconstruction-based LSTM-Autoencoder for Anomaly-based DDoS Attack Detection over Multivariate Time-Series Data
Methodology Used: LSTM-Autoencoder (LSTM-AE) with reconstruction-error thresholding for unsupervised anomaly detection
Limitation of the Paper: Evaluated only on reflection-based attack types; limited coverage of the full CICDDoS2019 attack diversity

Author Names: M. S. Elsayed, N.-A. Le-Khac, S. Dev, A. D. Jurcut
Title of the Paper: DDoSNet: A Deep-Learning Model for Detecting Network Attacks
Methodology Used: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) combined with an Autoencoder and Softmax classifier
Limitation of the Paper: Designed and validated only for SDN environments; generalization to traditional networks not tested

Author Names: D. Alghazzawi, O. Bamasag, H. Ullah, M. Z. Asghar
Title of the Paper: Efficient Detection of DDoS Attacks Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model with Improved Feature Selection
Methodology Used: Hybrid CNN + Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) with Chi-square-based feature selection
Limitation of the Paper: Accuracy (94.52%) is lower than several later hybrid/LSTM-based models; performance highly dependent on the feature-selection step

Author Names: M. Subrmanian, K. Shanmugavadivel, P. S. Nandhini, R. Sowmya
Title of the Paper: Evaluating the Performance of LSTM and GRU in Detection of Distributed Denial of Service Attacks Using CICDDoS2019 Dataset
Methodology Used: Comparative supervised classification using LSTM and GRU networks
Limitation of the Paper: Purely supervised approach with no anomaly-detection component for unseen attacks; GRU accuracy (92.5%) notably lower than LSTM (99.4%)

Author Names: A. L. Yaser, H. M. Mousa, M. Hussein
Title of the Paper: Improved DDoS Detection Utilizing Deep Neural Networks and Feedforward Neural Networks as Autoencoder
Methodology Used: Feedforward Neural Network stacked as an Autoencoder combined with a Deep Neural Network classifier
Limitation of the Paper: Feedforward autoencoder cannot model temporal/sequential dependencies present in network traffic flows

Author Names: R. Aydin
Title of the Paper: A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-Based Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Detection and Defense System Design in Public Cloud Network Environment (LSTM-CLOUD)
Methodology Used: LSTM-based signature detection module paired with a defense/mitigation module
Limitation of the Paper: Signature-based detection strategy limits the system's ability to identify novel or zero-day attack patterns

Author Names: A. K. Mousa, M. N. Abdullah
Title of the Paper: An Improved Deep Learning Model for DDoS Detection Based on Hybrid Stacked Autoencoder and Checkpoint Network
Dataset Used: SDN DDoS dataset and Botnet dataset
Methodology Used: Hybrid LSTM + CNN with a stacked autoencoder, combined with a checkpoint network for fault tolerance
Limitation of the Paper: Increased architectural complexity and training overhead from stacking multiple deep components; not evaluated on CICDDoS2019 directly

Author Names: W. Xu, J. Jang-Jaccard, A. Singh, Y. Wei, F. Sabrina
Title of the Paper: Improving Performance of Autoencoder-Based Network Anomaly Detection on NSL-KDD Dataset
Methodology Used: Deep autoencoder with feature reduction for unsupervised network anomaly/intrusion detection
Limitation of the Paper: Tested only on the older NSL-KDD dataset; does not address modern, high-volume DDoS traffic patterns found in CICDDoS2019

Author Names: H. Elubeyd, D. Yiltas-Kaplan
Title of the Paper: Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Automatic DoS/DDoS Attacks Detection in Software-Defined Networks
Dataset Used: CICDDoS2019 and a custom-generated SDN dataset
Methodology Used: Hybrid combination of 1D CNN, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Dense Neural Network (DNN)
Limitation of the Paper: Combining three deep learning components increases training/computational cost; accuracy varies noticeably between the two datasets used (99.81% vs 99.88%)

Author Names: A. Zainudin, L. A. C. Ahakonye, R. Akter, D.-S. Kim, J.-M. Lee
Title of the Paper: An Efficient Hybrid-DNN for DDoS Detection and Classification in Software-Defined IIoT Networks
Methodology Used: Hybrid CNN-LSTM model with XGBoost-based feature selection
Limitation of the Paper: Purpose-built for Software-Defined IIoT environments; feature-selection dependency may limit robustness to unseen/evolving attack types

Author Names: T. Singha, J. Jang-Jaccard
Title of the Paper: MSCNN-LSTM-AE: Hybrid Autoencoder Combining Multi-Scale CNN and LSTM for Network Anomaly Detection
Methodology Used: Two-stage autoencoder: Multi-Scale CNN Autoencoder (MSCNN-AE) for spatial features followed by an LSTM-Autoencoder for temporal features
Limitation of the Paper: Reported accuracy (93.76%) and recall (92.26%) are lower than several supervised alternatives; two-stage pipeline adds architectural complexity

Author Names: M. A. Ferrag, L. Maglaras, S. Moschoyiannis, H. Janicke
Title of the Paper: Deep Learning for Cyber Security Intrusion Detection: Approaches, Datasets, and Comparative Study
Dataset Used: Multiple benchmark datasets (CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD, and others)
Methodology Used: Comparative survey and benchmarking of deep learning architectures (including LSTM and Autoencoders) for intrusion detection
Limitation of the Paper: A survey/benchmark study rather than a novel detection framework; does not propose a combined LSTM-Autoencoder architecture evaluated on CICDDoS2019

Author Names: S. Yeom, C. Choi, K. Kim
Title of the Paper: LSTM-Based Collaborative Source-Side DDoS Attack Detection
Dataset Used: Simulated/collected source-side network traffic (IEEE Access study)
Methodology Used: LSTM-based classifier deployed collaboratively across multiple source-side detection points
Limitation of the Paper: Requires deployment and coordination across multiple source nodes, increasing system complexity; not evaluated on CICDDoS2019 or with autoencoder-based anomaly detection

Author Names: A. Saied, R. E. Overill, T. Radzik
Title of the Paper: Detection of Known and Unknown DDoS Attacks Using Artificial Neural Networks
Methodology Used: Feedforward Artificial Neural Network (ANN) trained on labelled traffic signatures
Limitation of the Paper: Shallow ANN lacks temporal/sequential modeling and unsupervised anomaly detection, limiting effectiveness against fully unknown (zero-day) attacks

Author Names: R. Doriguzzi-Corin, S. Millar, S. Scott-Hayward, J. Martinez-del-Rincon, D. Siracusa
Title of the Paper: LUCID: A Practical, Lightweight Deep Learning Solution for DDoS Attack Detection
Dataset Used: CICDDoS2019, ISCX2012, and other benchmark datasets
Methodology Used: Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with dataset-agnostic preprocessing for low-overhead traffic classification
Limitation of the Paper: Purely supervised CNN-based classification; no unsupervised/anomaly-detection mechanism, so it struggles to generalize to entirely unseen attack types

Author Names: M. A. Salahuddin, V. Pourahmadi, H. A. Alameddine, M. F. Bari, R. Boutaba
Title of the Paper: Chronos: DDoS Attack Detection Using Time-Based Autoencoder
Methodology Used: Time-based Autoencoder using reconstruction error over sliding time windows
Limitation of the Paper: Does not incorporate LSTM-based sequence modeling; detection accuracy is sensitive to the choice of time-window size

Author Names: A. M. Al-Eryani, F. A. Omara, E. Hossny
Title of the Paper: A Deep Learning GRU-BiLSTM for DDoS Attack Detection
Methodology Used: Hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) model for combined spatial-temporal feature extraction
Limitation of the Paper: High computational complexity from combining two recurrent architectures; not evaluated against fully unsupervised/zero-day attack scenarios

Author Names: I. Priyadarshini, P. Mohanty, A. Alkhayyat, R. Sharma, S. Kumar
Title of the Paper: SDN and Application Layer DDoS Attacks Detection in IoT Devices by Attention-Based Bi-LSTM-CNN
Methodology Used: Attention-based hybrid Bi-LSTM and CNN model for application-layer DDoS detection
Limitation of the Paper: Focused specifically on application-layer attacks in IoT/SDN settings; attention mechanism adds computational overhead, limiting real-time deployment

Author Names: M. Cui et al.
Title of the Paper: Multi-Class Intrusion Detection System in SDN Based on Hybrid BiLSTM Model
Methodology Used: Hybrid Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) model for multi-class DDoS/intrusion classification
Limitation of the Paper: Multi-class classification increases model complexity and computational cost; performance degrades for underrepresented attack classes

Author Names: H. Wang et al.
Title of the Paper: A New DDoS Attack Detection Model Based on Improved Stacked Autoencoder and Gated Recurrent Unit for Software Defined Network
Methodology Used: Improved stacked Autoencoder combined with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) classifier
Limitation of the Paper: Added architectural complexity from stacking autoencoder and GRU layers; recent publication with limited independent cross-dataset validation
